question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

'Hold someone's feet to the fire'
option_1: Agree upon a shared venture with full conviction
option_2: Take big risks without knowing the consequences
option_4: Insist that someone fulfil their promises or obligations
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Insist that someone fulfil their promises or obligations.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "hold someone's feet to the fire" means to pressurise someone to do what they have promised, or to make them accountable for their commitments. (किसी को अपने वादे निभाने के लिए बाध्य करना)

◦ Example: The voters will hold the minister's feet to the fire over his election promises.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (a shared venture), Option 2 (taking risks) and Option 3 (thinking over a proposal) do not match the sense of pressuring someone to keep a promise.

NOTE

• Related idioms of pressure/accountability: "take to task", "call to account", "bring to book", "put the screws on".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Apraisal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Apraisal" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Appraisal" (with double 'p'), meaning an assessment or evaluation of the worth, quality or performance of something/someone. (मूल्यांकन)

◦ Correct: The manager conducted the annual performance appraisal.

• Spelling key: AP + PRAI + SAL.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Affiliate" (to officially connect/associate with an organisation), "Affliction" (pain, suffering or a medical condition) and "Anxious" (worried/nervous) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "appraise" (to assess/evaluate) with "apprise" (to inform). "The boss appraised my work" vs "The boss apprised me of the news".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

The practice of having two or more spouses at the same time was quite common in the olden days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Polygamy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Polygamy" is the practice or custom of having more than one spouse (wife or husband) at the same time. (बहुविवाह)

◦ Example: Polygamy is prohibited under many modern personal laws.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Patricide" — the killing of one's own father.

• Option 2 "Patriarchy" — a social system in which men hold power and authority.

• Option 4 "Parochialism" — a narrow, limited outlook confined to one's own small area or concerns.

NOTE

• Related terms: Monogamy (having one spouse), Polygyny (one man with many wives), Polyandry (one woman with many husbands), Bigamy (marrying while already married to another).

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

It is easiest to stay calm than to protest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. easier.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" signals a comparison between two things, so the comparative degree "easier" is required, not the superlative "easiest".

◦ Correct: It is easier to stay calm than to protest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more easier" is a double comparative — always wrong.

• Option 2 "the easier" — "the" is not needed here.

• Option 3 "easy" (positive degree) cannot be used with "than".

NOTE

• Degrees of "easy": easy – easier (with "than") – easiest (with "the"). Use the comparative for two, the superlative for three or more.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Active community involvement _____________ a sense of belonging and contributes to the overall well-being of society.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. fosters.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fosters" means encourages, promotes or nurtures the development of something. Active community involvement fosters (promotes) a sense of belonging. (बढ़ावा देना / पोषित करना)

◦ Correct: Active community involvement fosters a sense of belonging ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "collects" (to gather), Option 2 "forgets" and Option 3 "fails" do not fit a positive, constructive context.

NOTE

• Synonyms of foster: nurture, promote, encourage, cultivate, nourish. "Foster" also means to bring up a child that is not one's own (a foster child).

question:
Select the appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I haven't seen him _______ last week.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. since.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With the present perfect ("haven't seen") and a point of time in the past ("last week"), the correct preposition is "since".

◦ Correct: I haven't seen him since last week.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "for" is used with a period/duration (for a week), not a point of time.

• Options 2 "to" and 4 "beyond" do not fit this structure.

NOTE

• Use "since" with a point of time (since Monday, since 2020, since last week); use "for" with a length of time (for two hours, for a week).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The mellow tune of the flute soothes me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. harsh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mellow" means soft, smooth, pleasant and gentle (of sound, colour or flavour). Its antonym is "harsh", meaning rough, unpleasant and grating. (मधुर का विलोम — कर्कश)

◦ Example: The mellow music became harsh when the amplifier failed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "quiet", Option 3 "golden" and Option 4 "lyrical" are not opposites of "mellow"; "lyrical" is closer to a synonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of mellow: soft, smooth, gentle, soothing, rich. Antonyms: harsh, rough, jarring, grating.

question:
The given sentence has an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

India is not on war with Pakistan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. not at.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct fixed expression is "at war", not "on war". So "is not on war" should be "is not at war".

◦ Correct: India is not at war with Pakistan.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "at Pakistan" and 2 "for Pakistan" wrongly change the preposition after "war" (it should stay "with Pakistan").

• Option 4 "not of" does not fit.

NOTE

• Fixed expressions with "at": "at war", "at peace", "at rest", "at ease". We say a country is "at war with" another country.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

A hospital's hygine is the standard against which cleanliness is measured.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. hygiene.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "hygiene", meaning the practice of keeping clean to maintain health and prevent disease. (स्वच्छता)

◦ Correct: A hospital's hygiene is the standard against which cleanliness is measured.

• Spelling key: HY + GIENE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "hygene", "higenie" and "hygeine" are all incorrect spellings of the word.

NOTE

• Related word: "hygienic" (adjective — clean and free from germs). Remember the order of vowels: h-y-g-i-e-n-e.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Sloppy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Dashing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sloppy" means careless, untidy or messy (in appearance or work). Its antonym is "Dashing", meaning smart, stylish and attractive. (फूहड़/लापरवाह का विलोम — बांका/स्मार्ट)

◦ Example: He changed from a sloppy dresser into a dashing young man.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Untidy" is a synonym of sloppy.

• Option 2 "Humid" (damp/moist) and Option 4 "Rough" are unrelated as antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of sloppy: untidy, messy, careless, slovenly. Antonyms: neat, tidy, smart, dashing, meticulous.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Some types of ________ suck blood.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. leech.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "leech" is a blood-sucking worm (an aquatic or land-dwelling annelid). The sentence about creatures that "suck blood" needs "leech". (जोंक)

◦ Correct: Some types of leech suck blood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "leach" — a verb meaning to drain away (minerals) from soil by water.

• Option 2 "latch" — a fastening/catch for a door.

• Option 4 "leak" — to let liquid/gas escape through a hole.

NOTE

• "Leech" (noun — a blood-sucking worm; also a person who clings to others for gain) is a homophone of "leach". Choose by meaning.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that has a grammatical error.

He will have to / knuckle up really seriously, / if he wants to / crack the upcoming deal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. knuckle up really seriously.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct idiom is "knuckle down" (to begin to work hard and seriously), not "knuckle up". So the segment should read "knuckle down really seriously".

◦ Correct: He will have to knuckle down really seriously, if he wants to crack the upcoming deal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "He will have to", "if he wants to" and "crack the upcoming deal." are all grammatically correct.

NOTE

• "Knuckle down" = to apply oneself seriously to a task. Do not confuse it with "knuckle under" (to give in/submit to pressure).

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The miracle of resurection is not medically proven.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. resurrection.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "resurrection", meaning the act of rising from the dead or bringing something back to life/use. (पुनरुत्थान)

◦ Correct: The miracle of resurrection is not medically proven.

• Spelling key: RE + SUR + REC + TION (one 's', double 'r').

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "ressurrection", "resurrecsion" and "ressurection" are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Related verb: "resurrect" (to bring back to life or into use). The Resurrection is a key event in Christianity (the rising of Jesus).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the given sentence.

Such specifications have revived our designers and manufacturers, whereas this new arrangement will free them.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. restrain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Free" means to release, set at liberty or unrestrict. Its antonym is "restrain", meaning to hold back, restrict or keep under control. (मुक्त करना का विलोम — रोकना/नियंत्रित करना)

◦ Example: The new rules restrain rather than free the designers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "senior", Option 3 "swatted" (hit sharply) and Option 4 "productive" are unrelated as antonyms of "free".

NOTE

• Synonyms of free (verb): release, liberate, let go. Antonyms: restrain, restrict, confine, imprison, bind.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Nagamani, a brave student, lodged a F.I.R. against the criminal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. a F.I.R..

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the sound, not the letter. "F.I.R." begins with the vowel sound "eff" (/ef/), so it takes "an", not "a". So it should be "an F.I.R.".

◦ Correct: Nagamani, a brave student, lodged an F.I.R. against the criminal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "student, lodged", "against the criminal" and "Nagamani, a brave" are all correct.

NOTE

• Use "an" before a vowel sound: an F.I.R., an M.A., an hour, an honest man. Use "a" before a consonant sound: a university, a one-rupee coin.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Disposed
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Retained.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Disposed" (as in "dispose of") means to get rid of, throw away or discard. Its antonym is "Retained", meaning to keep or hold on to something. (निपटाना का विलोम — रखना/बनाए रखना)

◦ Example: She disposed of the old papers but retained the important ones.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Minded" (attended to / objected), Option 3 "Detained" (held back / kept in custody) and Option 4 "Pretended" (feigned) are not opposites of "disposed".

NOTE

• "Dispose of" = to get rid of. Note also "disposed to" = inclined/willing. Antonyms of discard: retain, keep, hold, preserve.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

We had to study a poem of lamentation, especially for the dead, written by Thomas Gray.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. an elegy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "elegy" is a poem of serious reflection or lamentation, typically a mourning song for the dead. (शोकगीत / विलाप-काव्य)

◦ Example: Thomas Gray's "Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard" is a famous elegy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "an essay" (a piece of prose writing), Option 2 "a report" and Option 4 "an account" are not specifically poems of mourning.

NOTE

• Related terms: Ode (a lyric poem of praise), Sonnet (a 14-line poem), Epic (a long narrative poem), Eulogy (a speech of praise, often for the dead).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The team with a high motivation level succeeded in its project despite of the challenges it faced.
option_3: despite of the challenges it faced.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. despite of the challenges it faced..

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Despite" is never followed by "of". The correct forms are "despite" or "in spite of". So it should be "despite the challenges it faced".

◦ Correct: ... succeeded in its project despite the challenges it faced.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "The team with", "a high motivation level" and "succeeded in its project" are all correct.

NOTE

• Remember: "despite" (no "of") = "in spite of" (with "of"). Both mean "regardless of / notwithstanding".

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can complete the given sentence.

Recent research says that most of our cottage industries lack finance. Thus, they are ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. thrown out of gear.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "thrown out of gear" means thrown into disorder / disrupted / made to stop functioning smoothly. As the cottage industries "lack finance", their working is disrupted. (अव्यवस्थित हो जाना / गड़बड़ा जाना)

◦ Correct: Thus, they are thrown out of gear.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "taking somebody for a ride" (to deceive/cheat), Option 3 "worn and torn" (damaged by use) and Option 4 "under a cloud" (under suspicion/in disgrace) do not fit the sense of disruption due to lack of finance.

NOTE

• "Out of gear" = not working properly / in disorder. Related: "throw a spanner in the works" (to disrupt a plan).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

This boy performed / extremely good / in the / dance competition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. extremely good.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word modifying the verb "performed" must be an adverb, not an adjective. "Good" is an adjective; the adverb is "well". So it should be "extremely well".

◦ Correct: This boy performed extremely well in the dance competition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "This boy performed", "in the" and "dance competition" are all correct.

NOTE

• "Good" describes a noun (a good performance); "well" describes a verb (performed well). "He is a good singer" vs "He sings well".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Throughout human history, there have been numerous, strange and unexplainable events that have occurred on our (1)______. From mysterious disappearances to bizarre natural phenomena, these (2)_____ continue to captivate our imagination and spark curiosity. On 30 June 1908, a massive explosion (3)______ in the remote Tunguska region of Siberia. The (4)_____ of the explosion is still debated, but it is believed to have been caused by a meteor or comet. Another fascinating phenomenon, the Bermuda Triangle is a region in the western part of the North Atlantic Ocean where ships and planes have mysteriously (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. planet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage talks about strange events "throughout human history" and later refers to Siberia and the Atlantic Ocean — events across the whole world. So the events occurred on our "planet" (Earth). (ग्रह — पृथ्वी)

◦ Correct: ... events that have occurred on our planet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "home", Option 3 "country" and Option 4 "neighbourhood" are too narrow for events spread across the whole Earth.

NOTE

• "Our planet" is a common way to refer to Earth as a whole, matching the global scope of the passage.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Throughout human history, there have been numerous, strange and unexplainable events that have occurred on our (1)______. From mysterious disappearances to bizarre natural phenomena, these (2)_____ continue to captivate our imagination and spark curiosity. On 30 June 1908, a massive explosion (3)______ in the remote Tunguska region of Siberia. The (4)_____ of the explosion is still debated, but it is believed to have been caused by a meteor or comet. Another fascinating phenomenon, the Bermuda Triangle is a region in the western part of the North Atlantic Ocean where ships and planes have mysteriously (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. events.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank refers back to the "strange and unexplainable events" mentioned in the first sentence, so "these events continue to captivate our imagination" is correct. (घटनाएँ)

◦ Correct: ... these events continue to captivate our imagination and spark curiosity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "changes", Option 3 "advent" (arrival/beginning — used in singular with "the") and Option 4 "adventures" do not match "strange and unexplainable events".

NOTE

• A pronoun/determiner like "these" refers back to a previously named noun; here it points to "events", keeping the reference consistent.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Throughout human history, there have been numerous, strange and unexplainable events that have occurred on our (1)______. From mysterious disappearances to bizarre natural phenomena, these (2)_____ continue to captivate our imagination and spark curiosity. On 30 June 1908, a massive explosion (3)______ in the remote Tunguska region of Siberia. The (4)_____ of the explosion is still debated, but it is believed to have been caused by a meteor or comet. Another fascinating phenomenon, the Bermuda Triangle is a region in the western part of the North Atlantic Ocean where ships and planes have mysteriously (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. took place.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Took place" means happened or occurred. A massive explosion "took place" in Tunguska on 30 June 1908 — the natural collocation for an event happening at a specific time and place. (घटित हुआ)

◦ Correct: ... a massive explosion took place in the remote Tunguska region of Siberia.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "conspired" (secretly plotted) is wrong — an explosion cannot conspire.

• Option 2 "came about" and Option 3 "appeared" are grammatically weaker and less idiomatic than "took place" for a sudden explosion.

NOTE

• "Take place" is generally used for planned or scheduled as well as occurring events; it fits a dated historical event like the Tunguska explosion.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Throughout human history, there have been numerous, strange and unexplainable events that have occurred on our (1)______. From mysterious disappearances to bizarre natural phenomena, these (2)_____ continue to captivate our imagination and spark curiosity. On 30 June 1908, a massive explosion (3)______ in the remote Tunguska region of Siberia. The (4)_____ of the explosion is still debated, but it is believed to have been caused by a meteor or comet. Another fascinating phenomenon, the Bermuda Triangle is a region in the western part of the North Atlantic Ocean where ships and planes have mysteriously (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. cause.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The next line says it "is believed to have been caused by a meteor or comet", which tells us the blank is about what caused/produced the explosion. So "The cause of the explosion is still debated". (कारण)

◦ Correct: The cause of the explosion is still debated ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "commencement" (beginning), Option 2 "stages" and Option 4 "beginning" refer to a starting point, not to the reason behind the explosion.

NOTE

• The clue is the very next clause ("caused by a meteor or comet"), which mirrors the word "cause". Always use such contextual clues in cloze/fill-in-the-blank passages.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Throughout human history, there have been numerous, strange and unexplainable events that have occurred on our (1)______. From mysterious disappearances to bizarre natural phenomena, these (2)_____ continue to captivate our imagination and spark curiosity. On 30 June 1908, a massive explosion (3)______ in the remote Tunguska region of Siberia. The (4)_____ of the explosion is still debated, but it is believed to have been caused by a meteor or comet. Another fascinating phenomenon, the Bermuda Triangle is a region in the western part of the North Atlantic Ocean where ships and planes have mysteriously (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. disappeared.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bermuda Triangle is famous for ships and planes that have "mysteriously disappeared" (vanished without trace). The verb "disappeared" fits after "have mysteriously". (गायब हो गए)

◦ Correct: ... where ships and planes have mysteriously disappeared.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "invisible" is an adjective (not a verb) and cannot follow "have mysteriously".

• Option 3 "besotted" (infatuated) and Option 4 "concealed" (hidden by someone) do not fit the idea of vanishing on their own.

NOTE

• The passage began with "mysterious disappearances"; the final blank echoes this theme, keeping the passage coherent.

question: Which of the following raw materials is NOT used to prepare the baking soda?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Na2CO3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃). It is manufactured by the Solvay (ammonia-soda) process, whose raw materials are sodium chloride (NaCl), ammonia (NH₃), carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water (H₂O).

• Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃), i.e. washing soda / soda ash, is a product obtained from baking soda (on heating), not a raw material used to prepare it. (नाबार्ड नहीं — Na₂CO₃ कच्चा माल नहीं है)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Reaction (Solvay): NaCl + NH₃ + CO₂ + H₂O → NaHCO₃ + NH₄Cl.

• On heating, 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ (baking soda gives washing soda).

NOTE

• Baking soda is used in cooking, as an antacid and in fire extinguishers; washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) is used for cleaning and softening hard water.

question: In the South Indian temples, the pyramidal tower is called the _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is vimana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In South Indian (Dravidian style) temple architecture, the pyramidal tower rising over the sanctum (garbhagriha) is called the "vimana". (विमान — द्रविड़ शैली का पिरामिडाकार शिखर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Mandapa" — the pillared hall in front of the sanctum where devotees gather.

• "Shikhara" — the curvilinear tower over the sanctum in North Indian (Nagara style) temples.

• "Gopuram" — the ornate gateway tower at the entrance of South Indian temples.

NOTE

• Three main temple styles in India: Nagara (North — shikhara), Dravida (South — vimana and gopuram) and Vesara (Deccan — a hybrid style).

question: What is the duration for which a member of a House of Legislature of a State is, without permission of the House, absent from all meetings, thereof the house may declare his seat vacant?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 60 days.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the Constitution, if a member of a State Legislature remains absent for 60 days from all meetings of the House without its permission, the House may declare his/her seat vacant. (60 दिन — अनुच्छेद 190)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• This provision is contained in Article 190(4) for State Legislatures.

• A similar provision for Parliament exists under Article 101(4) (60 days' absence).

• In computing the 60 days, periods during which the House is prorogued or adjourned for more than four consecutive days are not counted.

NOTE

• Anti-defection and disqualification of members are dealt with under the Tenth Schedule and Articles 191–193 for the states.

question: Who among the following was the famous ruler of the Gauda Kingdom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shashanka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shashanka was the famous ruler of the Gauda Kingdom (in ancient Bengal), with his capital at Karnasuvarna. He is regarded as the first important independent king of Bengal (early 7th century CE). (शशांक — गौड़ राज्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shashanka was a contemporary and rival of Harshavardhana of Thanesar/Kannauj.

• He is said to have been involved in the killing of Rajyavardhana, Harsha's brother.

• "Grahavarman" was the Maukhari ruler married to Harsha's sister Rajyashri; "Rudradaman" was a Western Kshatrapa (Shaka) ruler famous for the Junagadh inscription.

NOTE

• Karnasuvarna (in present-day West Bengal) was Shashanka's capital; he was a follower of Shaivism.

question: What is the main purpose of the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)?
option_2: Investigating and reporting on financial transactions
solution_text:
The correct answer is Investigating and reporting on financial transactions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main purpose of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is to audit and report on the financial transactions (receipts and expenditure) of the Union and State Governments, ensuring public money is spent lawfully and effectively. (सीएजी — लेखा परीक्षा एवं रिपोर्टिंग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The CAG is provided for under Article 148 of the Constitution and is often called the "guardian of the public purse".

• The CAG's reports are examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament.

• Regulating tax collection is done by the CBDT/CBIC, and the budget is prepared by the Finance Ministry — not the CAG.

NOTE

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called the CAG the most important officer under the Constitution. The first CAG of independent India was V. Narahari Rao.

question: Eutrophication is a condition where excessive growth of algal bloom occurs on the surface of a water body because of abundant nutrients. Which of the following are the key nutrients for eutrophication?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Phosphorus and nitrogen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The key nutrients responsible for eutrophication are phosphorus and nitrogen. When these accumulate (often from fertilisers, sewage and detergents), they cause excessive algal bloom on the water surface. (यूट्रोफिकेशन — फॉस्फोरस और नाइट्रोजन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The algal bloom blocks sunlight and, on decomposition, consumes dissolved oxygen, leading to oxygen depletion and death of aquatic life (fish kills).

• Major sources: run-off of nitrogen and phosphate fertilisers, untreated sewage and phosphate detergents.

NOTE

• Eutrophication reduces dissolved oxygen (DO) and increases BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) in water bodies, degrading water quality.

question: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following.
option_1: The development of the cotton textile industry in Britain led to the decline of Indian textile producers.
option_2: Cotton clothes made in England had driven Indian clothes out of the markets of Europe and America in the beginning of the 20th century.
option_3: The Sale and Devang communities of South India were famous for weaving.
option_4: The first cotton textile mill in India was established in Bombay in 1854.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cotton clothes made in England had driven Indian clothes out of the markets of Europe and America in the beginning of the 20th century.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This statement is INCORRECT because English/machine-made cotton cloth had driven Indian handmade textiles out of European and American markets much earlier — by the early 19th century (1800s), not "in the beginning of the 20th century". (गलत कथन — समय-अवधि गलत है)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The other statements are correct: the rise of Britain's mechanised cotton industry ruined Indian handloom weavers; the Sale and Devang communities of South India were noted weavers; and the first cotton textile mill in India was set up at Bombay in 1854 (by Cowasjee Nanabhoy Davar).

NOTE

• The decline of Indian textiles under colonial rule is called de-industrialisation; it turned India into an exporter of raw cotton and an importer of British cloth.

question: The famous Jain temple of Dilwara, built by Solanki rulers, is located at which place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mount Abu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Dilwara Jain Temples, built during the 11th–13th centuries (under Solanki/Chalukya patronage), are located at Mount Abu in Rajasthan. (दिलवाड़ा जैन मंदिर — माउंट आबू)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The temples are renowned for their exquisite marble carvings on ceilings, pillars and arches.

• Key temples include the Vimal Vasahi (dedicated to Adinath, the first Tirthankara) and the Luna Vasahi (dedicated to Neminath), built by ministers Vimal Shah and the brothers Vastupala and Tejpala.

NOTE

• Mount Abu is the only hill station of Rajasthan (in the Aravalli range) and is an important Jain pilgrimage centre.

question: In December 2023, which former Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) CEO and MD joined the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IIT Bombay) as Head of Translational Research and Entrepreneurship?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajesh Gopinathan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In December 2023, former TCS CEO and Managing Director Rajesh Gopinathan joined IIT Bombay as Head of Translational Research and Entrepreneurship. (राजेश गोपीनाथन — आईआईटी बॉम्बे)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Rajesh Gopinathan served as the CEO & MD of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) from 2017 to 2023.

• Subramaniam Ramadorai and Natarajan Chandrasekaran were earlier CEOs of TCS; Chandrasekaran is currently the Chairman of Tata Sons.

• F. C. Kohli is regarded as the "Father of the Indian IT industry" and was the first CEO of TCS.

NOTE

• TCS, part of the Tata Group, is India's largest IT services company and among the world's most valuable IT brands.

question: 'Dollu Kunitha' is primarily a folk dance of which of the following Indian states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dollu Kunitha" is a popular drum dance and folk dance of Karnataka, performed mainly by the Kuruba community. (डोल्लू कुनिता — कर्नाटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Dollu" means a large drum worn around the neck, and "Kunitha" means dance; performers beat the drums while dancing in vigorous, synchronised movements.

• It is often associated with the worship of Lord Beereshwara (Shiva).

NOTE

• Other folk dances of Karnataka: Yakshagana, Veeragase, Kamsale and Nagamandala.

question: Who among the following was the first President of Indian National Congress?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Womesh Chandra Banerjee.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Womesh Chandra Banerjee (W. C. Bonnerjee) was the first President of the Indian National Congress, presiding over its first session held in Bombay in December 1885. (व्योमेश चंद्र बनर्जी — कांग्रेस के प्रथम अध्यक्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 with the efforts of A. O. Hume (a retired British civil servant).

• Dadabhai Naoroji ("Grand Old Man of India") was President three times; Badruddin Tyabji was the first Muslim President (1887); George Yule was the first English President (1888).

NOTE

• The first Congress session (1885) was attended by 72 delegates and held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay.

question: Which of the following States/Union Territories is included in the 'Areas of Inadequate Rainfall' of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ladakh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ladakh falls in the "Areas of Inadequate/Low Rainfall" of India. It is a cold desert lying in the rain-shadow of the Himalayas, receiving very little rainfall (often less than 50 cm/year). (लद्दाख — अपर्याप्त वर्षा क्षेत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Areas of very low rainfall (< 50 cm) include Ladakh, western Rajasthan, and interior Deccan/parts of Gujarat.

• Meghalaya (with Mawsynram and Cherrapunji) receives the highest rainfall in the world; the Andaman and Nicobar Islands also get heavy rainfall.

NOTE

• India's rainfall is classified as: areas of high rainfall (>200 cm), moderate (100–200 cm), low (50–100 cm) and inadequate (<50 cm).

question: Which of the following countries hosted the ACC Under-19 Asia Cup cricket in the year 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is UAE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ACC Under-19 Asia Cup 2023 was hosted by the UAE (United Arab Emirates). India won the tournament, beating Bangladesh in the final. (यूएई — अंडर-19 एशिया कप 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The U-19 Asia Cup is organised by the Asian Cricket Council (ACC).

• India lifted the title, continuing its strong record in age-group cricket in Asia.

NOTE

• The UAE, with stadiums at Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah, is a frequent neutral venue for Asian and international cricket.

question: According to the census of India 2011, which of the following states has the highest percentage of rural population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, Bihar had the highest percentage of rural population among these states — about 88.7% of its population lived in rural areas. (बिहार — सर्वाधिक ग्रामीण जनसंख्या प्रतिशत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• As per Census 2011, India's rural population was about 68.8% and urban about 31.2%.

• Himachal Pradesh and Bihar were among the most rural (least urbanised) states; Goa and Mizoram were among the most urbanised.

NOTE

• The Census of India 2011 was the 15th census since 1872 and the 7th after independence; the census is conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.

question: Coimbatore, which is located in the state of ________, is famous for the cotton textile industry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Coimbatore, located in Tamil Nadu, is famous for its cotton textile industry and is often called the "Manchester of South India". (कोयंबटूर — तमिलनाडु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Coimbatore's textile growth was aided by the Noyyal river, availability of cotton from surrounding regions, and hydroelectricity from the Pykara falls.

• Tamil Nadu leads India in the number of spinning mills.

NOTE

• Other textile centres: Mumbai and Ahmedabad ("Manchester of India"), Kanpur ("Manchester of North India") and Tiruppur (knitwear/hosiery hub, Tamil Nadu).

question: The Parliamentary form of Government is a key feature given in the Indian Constitution and its provisions are detailed in Articles _____________ of Part V (Chapter II).
solution_text:
The correct answer is 79 to 122.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Parliament of India and its provisions are detailed in Articles 79 to 122 under Part V (Chapter II) of the Constitution. (संसद — अनुच्छेद 79 से 122)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 79 — Constitution of Parliament (President + two Houses: Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha).

• Articles 124 to 147 — the Supreme Court (Union Judiciary).

• Articles 168 to 212 — the State Legislatures.

NOTE

• India follows the parliamentary (Westminster) system with a bicameral Parliament at the Centre — the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People).

question: Hampi Utsava is a colourful cultural festival that emulates the ethos and grandeur of which of the following empires?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vijayanagara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Hampi Utsava (also called the Vijaya Utsav) is a grand cultural festival held at Hampi in Karnataka that celebrates the ethos and grandeur of the Vijayanagara Empire. (हम्पी उत्सव — विजयनगर साम्राज्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire (founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty) and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• Famous monuments at Hampi: the Virupaksha Temple, the Vittala Temple (stone chariot and musical pillars) and the Lotus Mahal.

NOTE

• The greatest Vijayanagara ruler was Krishnadevaraya (of the Tuluva dynasty); the empire declined after its defeat at the Battle of Talikota (1565).

question: In June 2023, which state Government launched a project named 'Pride' to provide employment opportunities to the transgender community in diverse and innovative sectors?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2023, the Kerala Government launched a project named "Pride" to provide employment opportunities to the transgender community in diverse and innovative sectors. (केरल — 'प्राइड' परियोजना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kerala has been a pioneer in transgender welfare, having released India's first State Transgender Policy in 2015.

• Such schemes aim at the social and economic inclusion of transgender persons.

NOTE

• The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 provides for the rights and welfare of transgender persons at the national level.

question: Which of the following is a molecular compound?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CO2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• CO₂ (carbon dioxide) is a molecular (covalent) compound — it is formed by the sharing of electrons between carbon and oxygen atoms (non-metals). (CO₂ — आण्विक/सहसंयोजी यौगिक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• CaO (calcium oxide), NaCl (sodium chloride) and MgSO₄ (magnesium sulphate) are ionic compounds — formed by the transfer of electrons between a metal and a non-metal (or polyatomic ion).

NOTE

• Molecular/covalent compounds are usually formed between non-metals, have low melting points, and do not conduct electricity in the pure state. Ionic compounds are formed between metals and non-metals, have high melting points, and conduct electricity when molten or dissolved.

question: In India, documented by a study, in which level of education is the majority of the population unemployed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Graduate and post-graduate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Studies on unemployment in India show that the highest rate of unemployment is among the educated — the graduate and post-graduate population. This is often described as "educated unemployment". (स्नातक एवं स्नातकोत्तर — शिक्षित बेरोज़गारी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Educated unemployment occurs when qualified people cannot find jobs matching their qualifications, often due to a mismatch between skills and available jobs.

• Types of unemployment in India: disguised (mainly in agriculture), seasonal, structural, frictional and cyclical.

NOTE

• Unemployment data in India is collected through the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by the National Statistical Office (NSO).

question: Mangalampalli Balamuralikrishna was an Indian Carnatic singer born in Sankaraguptam village of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary Carnatic vocalist Mangalampalli Balamuralikrishna was born in Sankaraguptam village of Andhra Pradesh (in 1930). (एम. बालमुरलीकृष्ण — आंध्र प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He was a versatile musician — a vocalist, composer and player of instruments like the viola, violin and mridangam.

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri, among numerous other awards.

NOTE

• Carnatic music is the classical music tradition of South India; its "trinity" of composers were Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.

question: Which of the following are edible polysaccharides?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Starch, alginates, pectins and chitosans.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Starch, alginates, pectins and chitosans are all edible polysaccharides (large carbohydrate molecules made of many sugar units) that can be safely consumed/digested or used in food. (खाद्य बहुशर्कराएँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Starch is the main storage polysaccharide in plants (rice, wheat, potatoes).

• Pectins (from fruits) are used to set jams and jellies; alginates (from seaweed) are used as thickeners; chitosan (from chitin) is used in food and medicine.

• The other options include non-carbohydrate proteins (actin, myosin) or indigestible/structural substances (cellulose, chitin), so they are not purely edible polysaccharides.

NOTE

• Carbohydrates are classified as monosaccharides (glucose, fructose), disaccharides (sucrose, lactose, maltose) and polysaccharides (starch, glycogen, cellulose).

question: Who among the following is the author of the book 'The Hungry Tide'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amitav Ghosh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Hungry Tide" (2004) is a novel written by the acclaimed Indian author Amitav Ghosh. It is set in the Sundarbans region of the Bay of Bengal. (द हंग्री टाइड — अमिताव घोष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Amitav Ghosh won the Jnanpith Award (2018), the first English-language writer to do so.

• His other famous works include The Shadow Lines, The Glass Palace, Sea of Poppies and The Circle of Reason.

NOTE

• Ruskin Bond (The Room on the Roof), R. K. Narayan (Malgudi Days, The Guide) and Mulk Raj Anand (Untouchable, Coolie) are other celebrated Indian writers in English.

question: Odissi dancer ____________ was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2022 in the dance category.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Niranjan Rout.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Niranjan Rout, an exponent of the Odissi classical dance form, was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2022 in the dance category. (निरंजन राउत — ओडिसी — संगीत नाटक अकादमी पुरस्कार 2022)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is one of the highest honours for practising artists in the fields of music, dance and drama in India.

• Odissi is the classical dance form of Odisha, known for its graceful tribhangi posture and sculpturesque poses.

NOTE

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for the performing arts, was established in 1952; its highest honour is the Akademi Ratna (Fellowship).

question: In the year 2010, Commonwealth Games was hosted by which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 2010 Commonwealth Games were hosted by India, held in New Delhi from 3 to 14 October 2010. (2010 राष्ट्रमंडल खेल — भारत, नई दिल्ली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• It was the XIX Commonwealth Games and the first time India hosted the event; the mascot was "Shera" (a tiger).

• Australia topped the medal tally, while India finished second with its best-ever performance at that time.

NOTE

• The Commonwealth Games are held every four years among nations of the Commonwealth of Nations. The subsequent editions were held in Glasgow (2014), Gold Coast (2018) and Birmingham (2022).
